minutes.headline: Finance Committee heard the town manager's balanced FY17 budget with no override, then backed the Chapter 70 resolution.
minutes.summary: The town manager presented her preliminary FY2017 budget recommendation covering revenue, state aid, new growth, debt, insurance, retirement assessment and strategic investments. The committee asked questions on meals tax, Chapter 70, debt policy, Cadillac tax and retirement. It voted to recommend the Chapter 70 resolution, approved two sets of minutes and adjourned.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee voted to recommend that the legislature approve the Chapter 70 funding resolution; the motion passed.
The town manager presented a preliminary FY2017 budget recommendation with projected revenue growth and no override requested.
State aid was estimated to rise modestly, with any higher Chapter 70 amount from the governor going to the schools.
The capital committee recommended 12 items, and the first 10 were funded; debt service is rising but the net effect on the operating budget is about level.
The retirement assessment increase continues until 2040, and health insurance renews at the cap with a larger effect on the school side.

why_it_matters: The budget is presented without an override, so the tax question for residents turns on new growth, state aid and fixed costs such as retirement and health insurance, which keep rising.
The retirement assessment runs until 2040, so it takes a share of the town budget, mostly taxes, for many years before any new service is funded.
watch_next: The Chapter 70 resolution now goes forward as the committee's recommendation to the legislature.
The committee dropped the budget goals item from agendas during budget season, so watch the next agendas for the FY17 budget review.
